key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: It will have a material impact on near-term inflation through higher energy prices.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: This is also higher than the path in the December projections, mainly owing to higher energy prices feeding into inflation excluding energy and food.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: The risks to the growth outlook are tilted to the downside, especially in the near term.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: More volatile and risk-averse financial markets could weigh on demand and thereby lower inflation as well.

briefing:
The ECB kept its key interest rates unchanged. The Hawk & Dove stance index rates the press conference as slightly hawkish: it ranks at the 67th percentile of the 51 press conferences held since December 2019, up from the 42nd percentile at the previous meeting on 5 February 2026. The monetary policy statement ranks at the 71st percentile and the answers in the Q&A at the 47th.

The ECB expects inflation to average 2.6 per cent in 2026, 2.0 per cent in 2027, and 2.1 per cent in 2028 [1]. The economy grew by 0.2 per cent in the fourth quarter of 2025, driven by stronger domestic demand, with households increasing their spending as real incomes rose and unemployment remained close to its historical low [2]. The risks to the growth outlook are tilted to the downside, especially in the near term, due to the war in the Middle East and a prolonged war could increase energy prices further and for longer than currently expected [3].

The risks to the inflation outlook are tilted to the upside, especially in the near term, due to a prolonged war in the Middle East, which could lead to a larger and longer-lasting upward shift in energy prices than currently expected [4]. The ECB is concerned about the opacity, lack of transparency, and leverage of private credit and private equity instruments, and is keen to see the work produced by the European Commission on reviewing EU merger rules [5].
